Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the intro to Redwood's procurement team. Velvet Media is ready to kick off onboarding for our new supplier account, but we have a slightly unusual situation: we operate three registered business units in the US, each with its own EIN. Our AP team wants to confirm how Redwood prefers to receive tax proof for multi-entity vendors and which signer(s) you need on file to issue a consolidated PO.

Quick overview:
- Entity A (Velvet Media LLC): EIN 12-3456789
- Entity B (Velvet Media Digital LLC): EIN 98-7654321
- Entity C (Velvet Media Services LLC): EIN 22-3334445

We can supply separate signed W-9s for each entity or a single W-9 plus an internal matrix showing DBA/legal relationships. Which path will avoid blocking PO creation? Also, do you require notarized signatures for multiple EINs or is a corporate officer signature acceptable?

I've attached the draft W-9 for Entity A and a spreadsheet with the entity mapping.

Thanks,
Maya

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, that helps. Looping in Kimberly (vendor tax lead) and Ben (procurement ops) so we have the right reviewers.

Kimberly/Ben — quick context: Velvet Media is asking whether we need three fully executed W-9s or whether one W-9 plus a legal mapping matrix is acceptable for PO issuance. They'd like to avoid multiple notarizations if possible.

From procurement-side, here's what we typically need to clear a PO:
- Valid W-9 for the legal entity that will receive the PO (matching remit name and EIN)
- If the vendor invoices under a DBA, we need documentation mapping DBA -> legal entity
- Evidence of authorized signer (printed name, title on W-9). Notarization is rare for US entities unless KYC flags a mismatch.

If we accept a consolidated route, we need an attestation document from Velvet Media stating which entity will accept the PO and invoice. Otherwise we should collect a W-9 per EIN.

Maya — can you confirm which legal entity will be the payee for the initial PO? If they prefer a consolidated arrangement, a signed attestation (one page) is the quickest route. Ben, can you advise on whether our AP system can accept a single remit entity while tagging invoices from subsidiaries?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake

Jordan/Kim — quick operational note from AP: our purchase-order system can be tied to a single remit-to legal entity per contract. We can accept invoices from other Velvet entities if Velvet includes the remit-to legal name and the invoiced amount maps back to the PO. That means two viable paths:

1) Single-payee setup (faster): Velvet designates one legal entity to receive the PO and payments. Provide a W-9 for that entity and the multi-EIN matrix as supporting evidence. We'll also need a short attestation on Velvet letterhead confirming the arrangement and naming the authorized signer(s).

2) Multi-entity setup (slower): Submit a signed W-9 for each EIN and we create separate POs per entity. This adds processing time and may require separate contracting/invoice routing.

For our standard onboarding SLA, option 1 typically clears in 3–5 business days after we receive the signed W-9 + attestation + matrix. Option 2 can take 10+ business days.

Maya — if you can attach a one-page attestation naming the payee and the authorized signer, we can provisionally create a PO in our staging queue and move to active once final docs land.

Ben Carter
Vendor Operations | Redwood Inference
